title: learning_block's migrate keeps order, and a standing flat root announces itself
intention: learning_block's migrate writes a holder's file old lines first, then its own, each line once; and a flat trace root left standing raises the trouble learning-block-flat-root-stands on the first survey that misses it.
why: Measured 2026-11-16 on akiendelllinux: ticket 17d4d1899545 (PROVED 2026-11-13) moved traces under their holders and shipped migrate, but the verb never ran here. ~/.cairn/devices/learning_block/0/traces still held 16 files (~18,200 lines, all 351 historical finding events), trace_roots() does not read it, and every trace reader (tellmeabout's findings, the door-refusal probes, dial, clearance's read_attempts) counted from 2026-11-13 only. tellmeabout's seal reds on it. migrate as shipped would append that history after the holders' newer lines, and readers return a file in order. Nothing announced the standing root.
traces_to: Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces) and Law 5 (the address carries what a mind needs now, which includes the history the readers count).
how: migrate rewrites each holder file as flat lines then the holder's own, first occurrence kept, through a .migrating temp file and os.replace. learning_block gains flat_root() and announce_flat_root(); trace_roots() calls the latter after the CAIRN_LB_TRACE_ROOT short-circuit, raising through ModuleRaiser('learning_block') once per process with root, files and line count. One proof, every write under a scratch HOME.

clauses.claim: under a scratch HOME, migrate over a flat file [1,2,3] and a holder file [3,14,15] leaves the holder file [1,2,3,14,15], reports 2 new lines, removes the flat file and leaves no .migrating file

under a scratch HOME with a flat root holding 2 files and 3 non-blank lines, two trace_roots() calls in one process write exactly one raise_trouble emission with pointer learning-block-flat-root-stands, its detail naming the root, both files and 3 lines, its why naming migrate
no flat root, an empty flat root, or a survey over CAIRN_LB_TRACE_ROOT writes no learning-block-flat-root-stands emission

decisions.text: D1: migrate merges flat lines then holder lines, first occurrence kept, written to <dst>.migrating then os.replace; moved lines = merged minus what the holder had.

D2: learning_block.flat_root() is instance_path('learning_block', 0)/'traces'; announce_flat_root() raises FLAT_ROOT_TROUBLE = 'learning-block-flat-root-stands' via cairn.tools.base.diagnostic.ModuleRaiser('learning_block') (landing ~/.cairn/logs/learning_block/0/*.raise_trouble.json), once per process; trace_roots() calls it after the CAIRN_LB_TRACE_ROOT return. The module and trace_roots docstrings say so.
D3: proof cairn/machines/learning_block/proofs/test_migrate_keeps_order_and_a_flat_root_announces_itself.py, one tooth per clause, every write in a subprocess under a scratch HOME.

out: running migrate on any live box (an op after PROVED)
skills/tellmeabout (reseal only, after the live migrate)

measured.saw: the flat root ~/.cairn/devices/learning_block/0/traces holds 16 files, ~18,200 lines, 351 finding events; trace_roots() returns only the holder dirs, which hold 0 finding events
measured.how: wc -l and a json read of every file in both stores on akiendelllinux; lb.trace_roots()

measured.saw: migrate appends flat lines after a holder's existing ones; read_trace returns file order
the proof is 3/3 green on the build; on origin/main clauses 1 and 2 red, clause 3 green; 17d4's proof 5/5 over the build
measured.how: bin/cairn test --exec over each, and the proof copied into a detached origin/main worktree
